title: Unity in Diversity
definition: Unity in Diversity is the Church's calling to live as one body while honoring the different gifts, backgrounds, and roles God has given.
summary: Unity in Diversity teaches that Christ makes one body from believers with different gifts, backgrounds, cultures, abilities, and roles.
christFocus: Jesus Christ breaks down dividing walls and forms one new people through His cross.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine is not simply about getting along; it is about honoring God's intentional variety within one body. Diversity is received as stewardship, not threat, because the same Lord gives different gifts for the common good. Unity in diversity shows the wisdom of Christ in making people who are not the same genuinely belong together.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because churches often pressure people toward sameness or divide people by difference. The Gospel creates a unity deep enough to honor distinction without rivalry. This doctrine helps the church welcome disabled members, different generations, recovering people, rich and poor, mature and new believers, and many cultures without ranking their value.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Notice whose gifts, background, or limitations are being overlooked. Create space for different members to serve according to grace, not according to human preference. Repent of superiority, tokenism, and suspicion, and practice honor toward members unlike yourself.
